title: Know the BGR channel order
summary: OpenCV commonly uses blue, green, red order for colour images. Each uint8 channel can hold a whole number from 0 to 255.
introduction: OpenCV commonly uses blue, green, red order for colour images. Each uint8 channel can hold a whole number from 0 to 255. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain know the bgr channel order
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: OpenCV commonly uses blue, green, red order for colour images. Each uint8 channel can hold a whole number from 0 to 255.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

image = np.zeros((1, 1, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
image[0, 0] = [255, 0, 0]
print(image[0, 0].tolist())
blocks.title: Know the BGR channel order

blocks.text: The output is [255, 0, 0]. In OpenCV BGR order, this pixel is blue because the first channel is at its maximum.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Make the pixel red by moving 255 to the right channel.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Many other image tools use RGB order; check the order before passing images between tools.
For more detail later, use this [OpenCV further reading](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/d00/tutorial_py_root.html).
